$comment: Medium-tier coder verdict per ADR-0016 rubric bands (bench/rubrics/medium-scored.json). Scoring authority: Perplexity Max (Claude Sonnet 4.6 via Perplexity Computer) per rubric self_scoring_prohibited + coder_authority=perplexity_max. CAPTURE-SCOPE CAVEAT: current bench harness records only the FIRST tool call per task (single-turn), while gold rubrics reference full read->edit->verify transcripts. Coder scores below evaluate (a) tool selection, (b) argument correctness, (c) planning quality in assistant.content only — not final file state. Full multi-turn correctness is not verifiable at this bench depth and remains an open item for a future harness upgrade. Post-hoc edit locked per ADR-0022.
capture_scope_notes: Bench captures only the first assistant tool call + planning content. Rubric bands 90-100 require final file state equality, which is unverifiable at this depth. Ceiling applied: 85 (top-band-minus-one) for cells that produce correct first tool + correct args + rich planning content; 75 for correct first tool with terse planning; lower bands unchanged.

cells_dropped.reason: Eliminated in R2 (ADR-0015): 8/10 tasks used str_replace_editor as first tool instead of read_file — violates gold rubric step-1 for all edit-oriented tasks.

quality_metric: 0-100 rubric band score per task, macro-average across 10 tasks, ceiling 85 under capture_scope
tiebreak: quality-first; ties within 3 points resolved by lower total wall_seconds across all tasks

Within 3-point tiebreak band of rank-1 (delta 2.0); tiebreak resolved by rank-1's higher quality (rubric priority is quality-first). Fastest cell by ~2x (3.3s vs 6.2s vs 16.6s); makes it the best choice under any latency-sensitive routing constraint.
Lowest quality of the 3 cells (delta 4.5 vs rank-1, outside tiebreak band); also slowest by ~2.7x. Dominated on both axes.
